title: Dynamic Risk-Tranche Onboarding and Insurance Credit Experiment
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Goal: Run a controlled experiment that reduces friction for low-risk vendors while protecting Redwood by shifting insurance/contract terms into a dynamic, tranche-based model. Instead of a one-size SOC2 + fixed insurance surcharge, vendors can enter an onboarding path that places them into a risk tranche (A/B/C) based on automated evidence and manual review. Tranche A = fast-track (SOC2-lite + reduced insurance credit), Tranche B = standard (SOC2 evidence + standard insurance), Tranche C = high-risk (full SOC2 package + insurance escrow).

Why: Current onboarding creates a hard barrier for small vendors and integrations that are low-tech but low-risk, increasing cycle times and sales friction. We want to experiment with a pricing overlay (insurance credits) and a simplified SOC2-lite evidence flow to increase conversion while limiting Redwood's exposure.

Success metrics:
- +25% conversion from signed SOW to completed onboarding for low-complexity vendors within 30 days.
- No more than a 10% increase in median time to first incident for vendors in Tranche A during a 90-day pilot.
- Achieve net margin improvement on onboarding throughput (reduced manual review hours * labor cost saved - expected insurance premium delta) >= $1k/month after pilot scale to 50 vendors.

Scope: Product + PM + Legal + Security + Sales operations. Experiment includes: automated evidence intake form (vendor portal), risk-scoring ruleset, a manual-review escalation queue, an insurance-credit calculation that appears in quote, and contract appendix templates per tranche. Excludes: on-prem customers, customers requiring custom contracting or explicit gov/regulatory requirements.

Stakeholders: Legal (contracts/clauses), Security (SOC2 baseline & controls classification), Sales Ops (quotes & billing), Finance (insurance credit accounting), Eng (portal + automation), Solutions/SE (manual review).
acceptance_criteria: Portal exposes a single intake flow that assigns a vendor to Tranche A/B/C using the ruleset and logs rationale.
Insurance credit is calculable on quotes and reflected in the proposal PDF for Sales to send.
Manual review queue surfaces vendors flagged for escalation with checklist items for Security/Legal.
Contract appendix templates for A/B/C exist in Drive and are referenced by Sales Ops.
Pilot telemetry: conversion rate, time-to-onboard, number of manual reviews, and first-90d incident rate are all instrumented and visible in a shared dashboard.
Security sign-off obtained on SOC2-lite definition and acceptance criteria before rollout.
tasks: Design tranche ruleset and control mapping (PM + Security)
Build intake form in vendor portal (Eng) - minimal fields for tranche scoring
Create contract appendix templates and insurance credit language (Legal)
Wire insurance-credit calculation into quote flow (Sales Ops + Eng)
Create manual review queue UI and runbook (Eng + Security)
Run pilot with 25-50 vendors and collect data (PM + Sales)
Post‑pilot analysis and decision: scale, iterate, or rollback (PM + Finance + Legal)
Prepare communications and training for Sales/SE teams

notes:
Trade-offs discussed: 1) SOC2-lite increases residual risk; mitigating via shorter renewal cadence and insurance layer. 2) Pricing overlay complexity may confuse Sales; mitigate with clear quote UI and training. 3) If pilot shows incidents clustering in Tranche A, we will halt new Tranche A signups and triage existing vendors for reclassification.

Follow-ups: set up weekly 30-minute sync (PM/Eng/Security/Legal) for the pilot duration; capture any incident learnings in an incident playbook so we can adjust tranche thresholds quickly.
